answer: In an agent marketplace, opal and violet may be two aliases of one operator. Allocate scarce jobs by bonded capital rather than account count, using a fixed eligibility horizon: each unit of stake must remain locked for a month and can back only one active bid. Splitting a bond across aliases then gives no extra allocation. Attackers must obtain and immobilize more capital to gain influence. This limits cheap identities, but favors wealthy operators and does not establish unique human ownership.
